title: Jesus’ rebuke of Peter. Part 1
scripture_text: ‘’From that time on Jesus began to explain to his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, the chief priests and the teachers of the law, and that he must be killed and on the third day be raised to life. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him. “Never, Lord!” he said. “This shall never happen to you!”
devotional:
Jesus turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me; you do not have in mind the concerns of God, but merely human concerns.” Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me. For whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me will find it. What good will it be for someone to gain the whole world, yet forfeit their soul? Or what can anyone give in exchange for their soul? For the Son of Man is going to come in his Father’s glory with his angels, and then he will reward each person according to what they have done.’’

We want to look at how Jesus responded to Peter's rebuke and then consider the teaching that Jesus gave to counteract Peter's thinking. When we first read Jesus' reaction to Peter, it may appear a bit strong to us, but as we will see Jesus' response was both appropriate and necessary.

If we were to combine Matthew's account with Mark's we notice that Jesus does two things before He speaks.

Firstly, Jesus turned. Mark says, "When he turned!" It was as if Jesus was being led away from the other disciples, and before He spoke he turned and faced them. Here we have Jesus facing the situation head on. When we are involved in spiritual warfare, we need to be real and face things as they really are. Often in church life we skirt around issues, burying things under the mat of activity, hoping that they will go away. The only way we can overcome the temptations of Satan is to face them.

It is interesting to note that the word used for turn is the same word that is often used to describe person's conversion. It suggests a radical change of direction. The only way we can resist Satan is to constantly turn towards God and His purposes.

Secondly, Jesus looked at His disciples. Mark says 'But when Jesus turned and looked at his disciples,' Mark 8:33. He just didn't look at Peter, but at all the disciples. The Greek word for looked is ‘oida,’ which is a word that is derived from ‘eidoto’ to see, or perceive by means of the senses. This knowledge, however, is not deep, it lies near the surface of things. It carries the idea of ascertaining what must be done about a certain situation. So before Jesus speaks, he assess the situation so he can take the appropriate action.

Then Jesus rebukes Peter. In Greek, the common word for rebuke is ‘epitimao,’ " to rebuke, reprove, censure, also, to warn in order to prevent an action or bring one to an end.

The content of Jesus' rebuke.

Firstly Jesus identify Peter with Satan

Jesus doesn't call Pontius Pilate Satan. He doesn't call Herod Satan (a fox maybe but not Satan). Jesus doesn't call Caiaphas or Annias (the high priests), Satan. He calls one of his own Apostles, Satan. Why?

Peter’s rebuke was a repeat of the temptation that Satan offered Jesus in the wilderness. 'Again the Devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their splendour. All this I will give you, he said, if you bow down and worship me.' Matthew 4:8. In other words 'Jesus you don't have to suffer, you don't need to go to the cross. Or in Peter's words. 'This shall never happen to you.'

Peter's insistence upon an alternative to suffering is a satanic deception.

One of Satan's most effective weapons is not the sword but the velvet cushion. He comes to us and convinces us that we don't deserve suffering and pain, that we shouldn't have to suffer, especially for the needs of others. The belief that this life should be free from the humiliation of the cross is a satanic ploy designed to rob us of life. We need our crosses for the sake of others just as much as Jesus needed his cross for our sake.
prayer: Father help me to recognise that the desire and plan of Satan is to keep me from carrying my cross
